title: What is an exception
hook: An exception is an object derived from System.Exception, thrown with throw, that unwinds the stack until a matching catch or the thread dies. JavaScript can throw a string. C# will not compile that.

sections.heading: The CLR model
sections.prose: Microsoft’s exception overview is blunt: exceptions are types under System.Exception; throw creates a control transfer; the runtime walks frames looking for catch; if nothing handles it, the thread — and often the process — is finished. The object carries Message, StackTrace, InnerException, and sometimes HRESULT. You do not use exceptions for ordinary not-found on a hot cache lookup; you use TryGet or nullable returns. You do use them for broken invariants, I/O that cannot complete, and cancelled work (OperationCanceledException).

sections.heading: Versus JavaScript throw
sections.prose: JS throw 42, throw 'nope', throw { code: 500 } are all legal. catch (e) then guesses. TypeScript cannot fully close that hole. In C#, throw new InvalidOperationException("lease expired") is typed; catch clauses match on type (next topics). That is why a Node worker and a .NET SQS worker log failures differently: one may have a string, the other has a type you can filter.

snippets.label: Only Exception-derived throw
snippets.explanation: The compiler rejects throw raw or throw 401. Callers catch ArgumentException or let it bubble. AuthToken is the record from module 05.

sections.heading: What this module defers
sections.prose: If a Task faults and nobody observes the exception, that is an async story — unobserved task exceptions are module 13. If you thought a destructor would catch leaks, that is finalization — module 14. Here we stay on throw, catch, wrap, and Dispose.

interviewTakeaways: Unhandled exceptions unwind to the thread start; hosts may tear down the process.
Do not use exceptions for expected cache misses.
commonPitfalls: Translating JS habits: throwing strings or anonymous objects.
Using exceptions for control flow in a tight CSV import loop.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS exceptions are not a type hierarchy you can rely on. C# exceptions always derive from Exception.
TS catch (e: unknown) is the honest typing because throw is untyped. C# catch (ArgumentException ex) is exact.
